_readme: TWO PASSES, IN ORDER. Pass 1 is `inventory` — what is this source even about.
Pass 2 is `dimensions` — is it good enough to build from. Do not start pass 2 until
every inventory row is filled: a grade over a corpus you have not identified is a
grade of your own assumptions.
INVENTORY (pass 1), one row per file — EVERY file under sourceRoot, no format skipped —
filled by OPENING it:
kind:        docs | code | data | ui | contract | unknown
answers:     which dimension keys this source can speak to, e.g. ["domain","rules"].
Empty list is a real answer — say so rather than leaving it null.
statedScope: if the source declares its own boundary, quote it VERBATIM. Sources
that say what they do not cover are the cheapest scope signal there is.
components:  named modules/components/aggregates this source defines, one string each.
format/route/media/pages are stamped by init from bin/lib/source-formats.tsv — what the
file is by extension, the extraction route that consumes it whole, and how
many embedded images/diagrams a text-only read would leave behind. A row
with media > 0 is not consumed until its disposition accounts for them.
DISPOSITIONS (Stage 1) — one entry per inventory row (or a glob covering several), read
by bin/source-ledger.sh, which blocks the Stage 1 and 2 gates while any row has none:
{"path": "<rel>" | "pattern": "<glob over rel>", "state": "extracted",
"artifact": "<project-relative file or dir that carries what was extracted>",
"evidence": "<one specific finding that came OUT of the file, and where it landed>",
"media": <images described, must equal the row's media count, or "mediaWaived": "why">,
"by": "who", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
The artifact must exist, be non-empty, and NAME the source file — a disposition that
says 'the triage already used it' is checked by grepping the triage for the file, and
fails if it never mentions it. Write them with: bin/source-ledger.sh mark ...
A file deliberately not extracted is a register line, not a disposition:
bin/gate-check.sh <project> --waive source/<rel> --reason "..."
DIMENSIONS (pass 2). Fill in every dimension by READING the sources. Do not infer a
rating from file size.
rating: absent | named | specified | verified
evidence: where you saw it (page, section, screen) — or why you concluded absent.
consequence: what the BUILD has to invent if this stays as-is. Be concrete.
Leave rating null for any dimension you did not actually check; the report will
refuse to score rather than treat unchecked as absent.

dispositions.evidence: R-list: fast-track auto-approval (08 §4.4) vs manual-review-only (15 §11.4) contradiction -> brd F002 open question OQ-1

actors.demands: Who uses the system, and where one role's authority stops
actors.evidence: roles.md gives 4 roles with explicit authority (Shipping Agent, Berth Officer, Harbour Master, Inspector); 05-stakeholders-and-roles.html §2.3 states Harbour Master = Berth Officer + overrides/reactivation/tariff maintenance

domain.demands: Entities, their attributes, and the relationships between them
domain.evidence: 07-domain-overview.html, 12-berth-master-data.html, 14-vessel-registry.html, 26-audit-and-compliance.html, 36-appendix-data-dictionary.html give full typed attribute tables (11 entities) and an explicit relationships list with cardinality

processes.demands: Flows and sequences: what happens after what, and what state it leaves behind
processes.evidence: 08-booking-lifecycle.html status model, 15-officer-review-process.html queue/review, 16-approval-decisions.html outcomes, 22-25 inspection/departure flow all state concrete transitions
processes.consequence: two flows directly contradict each other — see rules

rules.demands: Business rules, validations, thresholds, calculations, eligibility criteria
rules.evidence: numeric thresholds throughout: 30-day max stay, 48h min / 90d max advance submission, 0.5m draught clearance, 120m fast-track length, 21% VAT, 15%/50% surcharges, flat 250/day shore power, 3-overdue-invoice auto-suspend, plus 2 screenshot-only validations (IMO=7 digits, rejection reason required)
rules.consequence: 3 direct contradictions found and NOT silently resolved — raised as open questions at Stage 2: (1) 08 §4.4 fast-track auto-approval vs 15 §11.4 'no automatic approval, manual review only'; (2) 13 §9.3 'only the Harbour Master may waive a tariff surcharge' vs 24 §20.3 'a berth officer may waive the late-arrival surcharge for vessels <80m'; (3) 10 §6.2 cancellation free until 24h before ETA vs 19 §15.2 cancellations within 72h of ETA charged 50% — the 24-72h window is claimed by both rules

ui.demands: Screens, navigation, layout, and which data appears on which
ui.evidence: 28-32 name every screen (Booking Board, My Bookings, Inspection Calendar, Officer Review Screen, Reporting) with fields/filters; 2 screenshots (09, 21) show validation states not in the prose

integrations.demands: External systems, protocols, credentials, and behaviour when they fail
integrations.evidence: 33-integration-ais-feed.html names the AIS feed, a 5-minute poll interval and the geofence-arrival behaviour
integrations.consequence: no protocol, auth, payload shape or failure-mode stated — open question for architecture

nfr.demands: Security, performance, availability, retention, data volumes
nfr.evidence: no performance, availability, retention or data-volume figures anywhere in the corpus
nfr.consequence: office hours (34-contact-and-support.html) is support-desk info, not an NFR

tenancy.demands: Whether one deployment serves many organisations, and how their data is isolated
tenancy.evidence: nothing states or implies multi-tenancy; corpus describes one port authority's own deployment

security_model.demands: The actor-to-permission mapping: who may do each thing, and who may not
security_model.evidence: roles.md + 05-stakeholders-and-roles.html §2.3 + 35-security-and-access.html ('agents can only see bookings, invoices and inspections that belong to their own company') give an explicit actor-to-permission map
security_model.consequence: the surcharge-waiver authority conflict above is also a security_model conflict (Harbour Master vs Berth Officer)

data_migration.demands: Existing data, its volume and shape, and how cutover happens
data_migration.evidence: requirements-driven entry mode, no legacy system or data anywhere in the corpus
data_migration.consequence: N/A by evidence, not by mode label — nothing to migrate

conflicts.title: Fast-track auto-approval vs manual-review-only
conflicts.detail: 08-booking-lifecycle.html §4.4 'Fast-track': a booking is automatically approved when the berth is free for the stay and the vessel is under 120m. 15-officer-review-process.html §11.4 'Manual review only': 'There is no automatic approval; every booking request is reviewed by a berth officer before it can become Approved.' Both are stated as settled requirements (Status: Agreed / no hedge).

conflicts.title: Surcharge waiver authority — Harbour Master only, or Berth Officer too
conflicts.detail: 13-berth-allocation-rules.html §9.3: 'Only the Harbour Master may waive a tariff surcharge.' 24-inspection-outcomes.html §20.3 'Surcharge relief': 'A berth officer may waive the late-arrival surcharge for vessels shorter than 80 metres.' The second is a specific case of the general rule the first forbids.

conflicts.title: Cancellation fee window overlaps itself
conflicts.detail: 10-cancellation-and-changes.html §6.2: cancellation is free of charge until 24 hours before ETA (implying free whenever cancelled earlier than T-24h). 19-tariffs-cancellation-fees.html §15.2 'Late cancellation': cancellations made within 72 hours of ETA are charged 50% of the berth fee. A cancellation between T-72h and T-24h is claimed as both free and 50%-charged.
